source_metadata_consequences: A saved hash of source_metadata.json binds the saved record, not perpetual presence of every path within it. Live metadata/storage verifiers may reopen .zattrs/.zarray/chunks or compare inode/ctime; archiving or restoring changes those operational identities. Retaining shapes alone does not keep a corpus qualified or usable. Preserve the complete archive and original metadata; issue fresh restoration/admission evidence when arrays are needed.
restoration: Byte-exact restore at original resolved paths can preserve current content/path based horizon identity. Recompression or relocation can change identity even with numerically equal arrays. New inode/ctime is not part of the horizon content digest but can invalidate separately pinned storage snapshots; do not edit old receipts. Reconstruct exact physical/schedule/qualification evidence only when a new consuming job needs it.

limits: No process or dataset inventory, deletion, archival, copy, runtime change, payload reads or tests.
